newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call rates fall on poor demand, good supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian call rates fall on poor demand, good supply.

text.p: Indian call money rates fell sharply on poor demand to end Tuesday at 3.00-3.50 percent against opening quotes of 5.00-5.25 percent, dealers said.
They said demand for cash was poor as banks had completed most of their borrowing ahead of the reporting day.
Banks report their positions to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Friday.
"Call rates will remain easy on Wednesday due to the good liquidity," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "They may move up a bit on Thursday due to repos auction outflows."
The RBI holds a repos auction on Wednesday and successful bidders make payment on Thursday.
"Given the current level of call rates, we may see good participation from banks...outflows could be 25 to 30 billion rupees," the dealer said.
Prices of government securities moved up slightly in moderate trade, dealers said.
Traded volumes on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) rose to 2.3 billion rupees from Monday's 1.58 billion rupees, they said.
"Most of the action was in securities maturing in 1999," said Vinld Dixit, dealer at Centurion Bank.
The 13.65 percent 1999 stock rose to 102.34 rupees from 102.32 while the 13.40 percent 1999 moved up to 101.70 rupees from 101.67, a dealer said.
